answer:
**Feature interactions explain why the same item appeals differently in different contexts.** A user liking hiking gear and an item being waterproof may be more predictive together than either feature alone. Recommendation architectures differ in how they represent such combinations. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.04247) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.13535) [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.00091)

Wide & Deep combines explicitly designed linear crosses with learned neural representations. The wide part can memorize a useful rule, while the deep part can generalize through embeddings. DeepFM adds factorization-machine pairwise interactions, using shared embeddings to learn which categorical values work together without storing every pair separately.

DCN explicitly constructs feature crosses across layers; DCN-v2 makes those interactions more expressive. DLRM embeds categorical inputs, processes dense inputs, and combines them through interaction operations before prediction. DHEN combines heterogeneous interaction modules so different forms of interaction can contribute at different depths.

**Compare the interaction mechanism, not just model size.** If a feature never arrives at serving time or its label leaks the outcome, no interaction network fixes the problem. Use the same data, features, and validation split for a fair comparison. Include calibration, embedding memory, feature-fetch latency, and p99 serving cost. A small log-loss gain may not justify a much heavier model in a stage that scores hundreds of candidates per request.

**Technical details and references.**

Wide & Deep combines a linear component over explicit crosses with a neural component. DeepFM shares embeddings between factorization-machine pairwise interactions and a DNN. DCN explicitly builds feature crosses; DCN-v2 increases expressiveness and supports low-rank/mixture variants. DLRM combines dense features with categorical embeddings and interaction operations. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.04247) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.13535) [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.00091)

DHEN ensembles heterogeneous interaction modules across depth to represent different interaction patterns; more modules add capacity and serving cost. The architectures address how features interact, not missing data quality or biased labels.

Compare identical input features, training samples, calibration, and latency. Embedding memory and feature retrieval can dominate the interaction network. A model that improves log loss may still be unsuitable if it exceeds the ranking stage's tail-latency budget.
